sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della guerra in corso tra Israele e Iran, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sceso a 18,20, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15, indicando una certa incertezza. L'S&P 500 è salito dell'1,18%, ma il DXY è aumentato dello 0,14%, segno di una maggiore avversione al rischio. Il prezzo del petrolio è salito dello 0,85%, ulteriore segnale di incertezza.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the ongoing war between Israel and Iran, negatively impacting equity markets and increasing demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX decreased to 18.20 but remains above 15, indicating some uncertainty. The S&P 500 rose by 1.18%, but the DXY increased by 0.14%, signifying greater risk aversion. Oil prices rose by 0.85%, further signaling uncertainty.

market_impact_summary.it: La guerra tra Israele e Iran continua a pesare sui mercati. L'S&P 500 è salito dell'1,18% a 6967,38, mentre il VIX è sceso dello 0,87% a 18,20. Il DXY è aumentato dello 0,14% a 98,25, segno di una maggiore avversione al rischio. Il prezzo del petrolio è salito dello 0,85% a $95,60. I tassi dei bond USA a 10 anni sono scesi dello 0,95% a 4,25%.
market_impact_summary.en: The war between Israel and Iran continues to weigh on markets. The S&P 500 rose by 1.18% to 6967.38, while the VIX decreased by 0.87% to 18.20. The DXY increased by 0.14% to 98.25, signifying greater risk aversion. Oil prices rose by 0.85% to $95.60. US 10-year bond yields fell by 0.95% to 4.25%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con risultati contrastanti. Il Nikkei ha guadagnato lo 0.4% a 58,134 punti, mentre lo Shanghai ha chiuso invariato a 4000 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha registrato un aumento dello 0.3% a 25,947 punti. Questi risultati lasciano intravedere una possibile apertura cauta in Europa.

Nella seduta di martedì, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dell'1.2% a 7000 punti. Il Dollar Index (DXY) è salito dello 0.1% a 98. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, è sceso dello 0.9% a 18. I tassi di interesse sono stati oggetto di attenzione: il TLT Bond USA 20Y ha guadagnato lo 0.5% a 87, mentre il rendimento del decennale USA è sceso dello 0.9% a 4.2%. L'oro è salito dello 0.2% a $4800 l'oncia. Il mercato sta manifestando un sentiment risk-off.

Sul fronte geopolitico, diverse notizie stanno impattando sui mercati. La possibile escalation del conflitto in Medio Oriente potrebbe rallentare la crescita globale al livello più basso dal periodo della pandemia, secondo il Fondo Monetario Internazionale. Le esportazioni cinesi stanno rallentando a causa della turbolenza nella regione. Inoltre, le dichiarazioni di Yellen riguardo alle proposte di Trump per tagliare i tassi d'interesse negli Usa stanno generando dibattiti.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, gli investitori attendono con ansia i prossimi dati sul PIL degli Usa, in uscita il 29 aprile. In precedenza, il tasso di disoccupazione negli Usa era del 4.3%, mentre il PCE Core YoY era al 3%. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse stabili, con un tasso dei depositi al 2%. La liquidity globale, misurata dal Global M2, continua ad espandersi, con un aumento del 4.9% su base annua.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. 
  Tecnicamente, dopo il rally degli ultimi mesi, il prezzo si è stabilizzato intorno ai 74.200 dollari, con un lieve calo dello 0.2% odierno. 
  Sul fronte degli ETF, registriamo un afflusso netto giornaliero di 411 milioni di dollari, segno di un interesse ancora vivo da parte degli investitori istituzionali.

  Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum scambia a 2.334 dollari, in calo dell'1.6%, mentre Solana e Binance Coin mostrano perdite più significative, rispettivamente del 2.7% e stabilità con un lieve aumento dello 0.4%, con prezzi di 84 dollari e 619 dollari.

  Per quanto riguarda il sentiment, l'indice Fear & Greed è a 23, in territorio di Extreme Fear. 
  Storicamente, livelli estremi di fear possono rappresentare un'opportunità di acquisto per gli investitori più esperti. 
  La correlazione con i mercati macro è ancora evidente, considerando i recenti dati economici USA che hanno mostrato un'inflazione ancora alta e un mercato del lavoro resiliente, ma con un'attenzione crescente verso le mosse future delle banche centrali.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off today, as indicated by the mixed performance across various asset classes. The VIX index is slightly lower, but still elevated at 18, suggesting that investors are cautious.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. The S&P 500 index is up 1.2% at 7,000, while the STOXX 600 is flat at 62. The Nikkei 225 index in Japan rose 0.4% to 58,134, while the Shanghai Composite and Hang Seng indices also saw modest gains. In the currency markets, the EUR/USD pair is up 0.1% at 1.2, while the Dollar Index (DXY) is also up 0.1% at 98. Commodities are mostly higher, with Brent crude oil up 0.8% at $96 and gold up 0.2% at $4,800 per ounce. Bond yields are lower, with the US 10-year yield down 0.9% at 4.2% and the TLT Bond USA 20Y up 0.5% at 87.

On the macro front, investors are closely watching the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, with Iran's potential involvement in the conflict weighing on global growth prospects. The IMF warned that a war in Iran could slow global growth to its weakest since the pandemic. In the US, attention is focused on the upcoming PCE Core YoY data, which is expected to provide insights into the country's inflation trajectory. In Europe, the recent rate hike by the ECB has been a key topic of discussion, with some analysts questioning the impact on the region's economic growth.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 

The recent surge in Bitcoin ETF daily net inflows, with a notable $411 million influx, has been a significant development. This comes as Bitcoin's price remains steady around $74,208, down 0.2% from the previous day. 

In the altcoin space, we're seeing mixed movements. Ethereum's price has dipped 1.6% to $2,334, while Solana and Binance Coin have seen declines of 2.7% and an increase of 0.4% respectively. 

The Fear & Greed Index currently stands at 23, indicating extreme fear in the market. This sentiment is reflective of the broader economic data, including the recent CPI and Non-Farm Payrolls reports from the US, which have shown mixed results. 

On the regulatory and adoption front, there's been notable progress. SocGen has launched a MiCA-compliant stablecoin, and Pakistan has begun allowing banks to serve licensed crypto firms, signaling a shift in their stance on cryptocurrency. 

These developments, along with the increasing institutional interest in crypto, as evidenced by the significant inflows into Bitcoin ETFs, suggest a complex and evolving market landscape.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with more market insights. Keep an eye on the key events and data releases that could impact your trades. Until then, stay informed and stay ahead. A final word from Prais Alért. See you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
articles.snippet: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in an unstable ceasefire, has exposed a structural failure in the global semiconductor memory supply chain, and it is not the one analysts seem to be tracking. The story receiving attention is helium: Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility went offline, a 45-day inventory clock started running, and spot prices doubled within days. The story receiving almost no attention is bromine, and it is potentially the more dangerous one. articles.title: Hungary Turns a New Page
articles.snippet: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán conceded defeat in a parliamentary election on April 12, ending his 16 years in power, after his Fidesz party lost its majority in parliament. The center-right Tisza party, led by Péter Magyar, won and is projected to have a two-thirds supermajority. Orbán has been a prominent right-wing populist, with close ties to the Trump administration in Washington and warm relations with Moscow. Magyar campaigned on promises to address corruption, improve the economy, and align more closely with Europe.We asked five experts to assess how the election results will shape Hungary’s role in Europe and its relationships The post Hungary Turns a New Page appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: The Rare Earth Trap: How China Outmaneuvered the Entire Western Defense Industry

But then REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) came along with partners and started building domestic processing capability while most of the industry was still looking the other way.…

articles.title: Europe’s Electrification Dream Is Hitting a Wall
articles.snippet: The message given by Ursula von der Leyen to electrify the European economy is strategically coherent, politically appealing, and, on the surface, even unavoidable. It will be the real deal to decarbonize industry and power transport, reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, and anchor Europe’s competitiveness. The latter is especially valid in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical order. Electrification is presented as the backbone of Europe’s future prosperity and security. However, beneath this clear vision lies a far more uncomfortable…

articles.title: Indonesia Turns to Russia for Oil as Middle East Risks Mount
articles.snippet: Indonesia and Russia are in talks on boosting cooperation, including through the long-term supply of Russian crude to the Asian nation, media have reported, following a meeting between the presidents of the two countries earlier this week. articles.title: China’s Petrochemical Sector Cuts Output as Costs Climb
articles.snippet: Chinese petrochemical makers have started idling capacity as the cost of their feedstocks rises amid the Middle East war, Bloomberg has reported, noting that output is down to the lowest in three years. About a fifth of the country’s petrochemicals capacity has been taken offline, the publication wrote today, citing data from a Chinese industrial news outlet. The report added that the petrochemicals industry is currently operating at just 68% of capacity. The futures prices of purified terephthalic acid, a chemical that is used in the production…
